$comment: PE/COFF relocatable object (.obj) for x86_64 Windows. Second shipped object-format JSON (plan 14 LK2 cycle 1, 2026-05-29). Consumed by `src/link/format/pe.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. Section Characteristics + IMAGE_FILE_HEADER fields + IMAGE_RELOCATION type values follow the Microsoft PE/COFF spec (PE Format on Microsoft Learn).
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: this artifact form has NO image header field for a stack size (a relocatable object / static archive is an INPUT to a later link, not a loadable program), so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request against it is REFUSED with an actionable remedy -- request the reserve on the build that produces the final EXECUTABLE image -- rather than silently dropped.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit Windows is LLP64 (int 32, long 32, long long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c-subset long binds I32 here, the literal ladder + descriptor signatureByDataModel resolve their LLP64 arms. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Windows filesystems (NTFS, FAT) match file names case-INSENSITIVELY, and the Windows SDK depends on it -- sqlite3.c:67322 spells `#include <Windows.h>` with a capital W while the shipped descriptor is `windows.json`. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) instead of asking fs::exists, so this resolves identically whether the build host is NTFS or ext4 -- MEASURED before the axis existed: rc=0 through /mnt/c, rc=1 error[F001A] on ext4, SAME binary, SAME commit.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: PE/COFF x64 applies NO decoration to a C identifier. The leading-underscore cdecl convention belongs to 32-bit x86 PE, which DSS does not ship; the 32-bit `_func` and stdcall `_func@N` rules arrive as their own scheme enumerators WITH their engine arms, never as a re-spelling of this one. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, GNU binutils via WSL): the UCRT exports `exit`, `_exit` AND `_Exit` as three DISTINCT entries -- so the underscored spelling is not a decoration of `exit` here either, it already names a different function, and a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would silently bind to it. Consistent with this family's own `processExit.importMangledName`, the undecorated `exit`. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): THIS FORMAT DELIBERATELY DECLARES NO `predefinedMacros`, and the absence is an ANSWER rather than an omission -- it is the whole reason the channel lives on the FORMAT and not on the target. `dataModel` above is LLP64, so `__LP64__`/`_LP64` must NOT be defined here: MEASURED 2026-07-30, `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (Apple clang 21.0.0) defines NEITHER, while the SAME clang defines BOTH on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-apple-darwin -- the same CPU, differing only by object format, which is precisely why a target-side row would be a lie on this leg. Adding either spelling here would make the Windows headers take their LP64 arms against a 32-bit `long`. Pinned in the NEGATIVE direction by tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: MSVC x64 bit-field packing (byte-ABI-exact to cl.exe). The strategy is OS/format-determined (x86_64 serves both PE and ELF), so it lives on the format, not the target. See pe64-x86_64-windows-exec for the full rule.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: MSVC x64 `long double` IS `double` (64-bit IEEE, 8/8) — the f64 axis collapses the c-subset `long double` row to F64. See pe64-x86_64-windows-exec for the full rationale.
$externCallDispatchComment: D-LK-OBJECT-EXTERN-CALL-RELOCATABLE (PE/COFF arm, c148 — the PE analog of the ELF c141 + Mach-O c146 closures): extern FUNCTION calls lower into this relocatable .obj as a plain direct `call rel32` (E8 disp32, zero patch bytes) + an IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32 relocation against an UNDEFINED COFF symbol (SectionNumber=0, StorageClass=EXTERNAL) carrying its REAL import name — PE x64 C mangling is IDENTITY (applyCMangling adds no leading underscore, unlike Mach-O), so `puts` is emitted verbatim. That rel32-CALL-against-undefined-symbol shape is the standard COFF contract: the FINAL linker (link.exe / lld-link) resolves it either directly to a same-link definition or through an import thunk it synthesizes for a DLL import — DSS never builds a stub/thunk inside a `.obj` (thunk synthesis is the EXEC walker's job, D-FFI-PE-IMPORT-THUNK). `direct-plt` is the declared verb because the call-site byte shape is the direct-call form (the ELF/Mach-O relocatable formats declare the same value for the same reason).
$weakDefinitionComment: D-CONFIG-WEAK-DEFINITION-DIALECT-NOT-DECLARED: HOW this format spells a WEAK DEFINITION -- a symbol several translation units may define, of which the linker keeps one. COFF has NO per-symbol weak storage class for a DEFINITION: IMAGE_SYM_CLASS_WEAK_EXTERNAL + its Auxiliary Format 3 record is a weak *REFERENCE* with a fallback alias (EXTERNAL storage class, UNDEF section number, value zero -- the /ALTERNATENAME shape), and it serves the separate ALIAS path. A weak DEFINITION here is a section flagged IMAGE_SCN_LNK_COMDAT whose Selection byte is IMAGE_COMDAT_SELECT_ANY -- "any section that defines the same COMDAT symbol can be linked; the rest are removed" -- which is exactly the semantics SymbolBinding::Weak carries. Verified against the published PE/COFF format, sections "Auxiliary Format 3: Weak Externals" and "COMDAT Sections (Object Only)"; the measured reference encodings that fix this choice (and the round trip through DSS's own COFF reader) live in the writer's weak-definition block in src/link/format/pe.cpp. THIS IS A DIALECT ROW, NOT A CAPABILITY FLAG: it says how this format spells something it CAN express, never that it cannot -- see D-LK-PE-ALTERNATENAME-DECLARE-AND-REFUSE for why an implementation gap recorded as a format incapability is a false fact in the place most likely to be trusted later. The .obj writer READS this key and refuses loud on a dialect it has no encoder for, so the declaration cannot drift away from what is actually emitted.
$sehPersonalityOmittedComment: UCRT-P4 (D-WIN64-SEH-FUNCLETS + D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): THIS FORMAT DELIBERATELY DECLARES NEITHER `sehPersonality` NOR `runtimeLibraries`, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE ANSWER RATHER THAN AN UNFINISHED COPY OF THE exec/dll SIBLINGS. Read this before adding either key, because the `synthesizeSehFunclets` diagnostic that fires without them ends with the advice 'Add the block', and FOLLOWING THAT ADVICE HERE PRODUCES A SILENT MISCOMPILE. * WHAT IS TRUE, AND IT IS A REAL DIVERGENCE WE ARE NOT MINIMISING: a `__try` in a translation unit compiled for x86_64:pe64-x86_64-windows is REFUSED (MEASURED 2026-08-10, rc=1, `synthesizeSehFunclets: 1 SEH region(s) resolved but object format 'pe64-x86_64-windows' declares NO sehPersonality block`), while MSVC compiles the same source to a .obj happily. A relocatable object CAN contain __try as far as the SOURCE is concerned, so this is a wrong-reject a user could hit. * WHY IT IS STILL THE RIGHT ANSWER, MEASURED THE ONLY WAY THAT SETTLES IT -- BY DECLARING THE TWO KEYS AND LOOKING AT THE BYTES: with them declared the compile SUCCEEDS rc=0 and the emitted seh.obj contains `.text` AND NOTHING ELSE -- no `.pdata`, no `.xdata`. `pe::encode`'s Obj arm attaches no FrameUnwindInfo (AssembledFunction::unwind is nullopt on the object path by construction) and SehScopeEntry is consumed ONLY by the image-side `.xdata` scope-table emitter in encodeExec, so the synthesized filter funclets and the scope table are DROPPED WITHOUT A WORD. The object links, the program runs, and the `__except` body can never execute -- a fault inside the guarded range walks past a handler that is not in any unwind table. Note this is strictly worse than the honest refusal precisely BECAUSE the object is meant for a later link: the final linker has no way to notice that the unwind data for these functions was never emitted. That trades a loud, correct refusal for a silent miscompile, which is the single outcome this project's bar rules out unconditionally, so the refusal STAYS until the Obj arm can carry unwind info. Contrast the .dll sibling, which DOES declare both keys and is witnessed: it routes through the SAME encodeExec substrate as the .exe, MEASURED to emit both sections, and a real Windows process loading a DSS-built .dll took a hardware divide-by-zero and resumed in the __except body at both --config=debug and --config=release. * `runtimeLibraries` is absent as a CONSEQUENCE, not as a second decision: with no `sehPersonality`, no `processExit`, no `processArgs` and no `librarySynthesis` on this format, NO block would name a role, and the loader refuses a table row that no block names as inert config. An empty table is the only self-consistent state. * ENFORCED, not merely written: tests/link/test_runtime_library_roles.cpp `NoPeFormatNamesTheLegacyCrtInItsRoleTable` carries this format on an EXPLICIT exclusion list and asserts BOTH that the two keys stay absent AND that this rationale key stays non-empty -- so the day the Obj arm gains unwind support and the keys land here, that test goes red and forces the exclusion to be re-argued rather than silently widened.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE/COFF arm, c148 — the PE analog of the ELF c142 + Mach-O c147 `.o` data sections): a relocatable .obj DOES carry data — a global lands in `.rdata`/`.data`/`.bss` with a section-relative IMAGE_SYMBOL (SectionNumber = the section's 1-based ordinal, Value = the item's SECTION-RELATIVE offset — the COFF convention, unlike Mach-O's flat-address n_value) the FINAL linker binds. Same format-blind `AssembledModule.dataItems` producer path as ELF/Mach-O. D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (PE arm): a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations (a const function-pointer table / `int *const p = &x;` — sqlite's VFS method tables + `aSyscall[]`) lands in `relro` = a SECOND `.rdata`-named section (see the relro row) and the writer emits its OWN IMAGE_RELOCATION table (IMAGE_REL_AMD64_ADDR64, addend IN the 8-byte slot bytes — COFF's in-place-addend convention; IMAGE_RELOCATION has no addend column); a reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer global lands in `data`. TLS (`tdata`/`tbss`) stays UNDECLARED — the linker's acceptsDataSection gate rejects it loud (the .obj walker emits no `.tls`/IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY64 machinery; that is the PE EXEC arm, D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL C3).

pe.$comment: IMAGE_FILE_HEADER identity. machine = IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64 (0x8664). characteristics = 0 — relocatable .obj carries no file-level flags (link.exe sets image-level flags when producing the .exe/.dll).

sections.$comment: Executable code. PE Characteristics = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE (0x20) | IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_16BYTES (0x500000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE (0x20000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) = 0x60500020. PE's `type` field is repurposed to carry Characteristics (which encodes alignment via IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_*BYTES bits); `flags` is unused; `addrAlign` MUST be 0 for PE rows (validate-rejected — PE encodes alignment in Characteristics, not the substrate's `addrAlign` field).
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): read-only initialized data (string literals, const globals WITHOUT relocations) — exactly where cl.exe places it in a .obj. Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x40) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) = 0x40000040 = 1073741888 — DELIBERATELY WITHOUT IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_*BYTES bits: the .obj walker ORs in the align class computed from the H1-raised layout alignment (max of every member item's alignment) at emit time, exactly the per-contribution align class cl.exe itself stamps (e.g. an 8-byte-aligned .rdata contribution carries 0x40400040). addrAlign MUST stay 0 (validate-rejected on PE rows — alignment lives in Characteristics, never the substrate field).
sections.name: .rdata

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): writable initialized data (mutable globals, `int counter = 7;`). Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x40) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE (0x80000000) = 0xC0000040 = 3221225536 — no align bits (walker-computed; see the rodata row). A reloc-bearing MUTABLE pointer global also lands here and the walker emits its IMAGE_RELOCATION records against this section (VirtualAddress = the slot's section-relative offset).
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: D-LK-OBJECT-DATA-SECTION-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): zero-initialized data (tentative globals `int g;` — DSS commits tentatives to a real `.bss` definition, the gcc -fno-common shape, NOT the MSVC COMMON-symbol form). Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA (0x80) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE (0x80000000) = 0xC0000080 = 3221225600 — no align bits (walker-computed). COFF .obj header convention (cl.exe-witnessed, dumpbin-confirmed): the bss span lives in SizeOfRawData with PointerToRawData = 0 and VirtualSize = 0 — the FILE stores no bytes; the final linker reserves SizeOfRawData zero-fill bytes.
sections.name: .bss

sections.$comment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (PE arm, c148): relocated-read-only const data — a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations (a const function-pointer table / `int *const p = &x;`). COFF has NO relro segment concept: MSVC places reloc-bearing const data in read-only `.rdata` and the LINKED image base-relocates it (the loader applies IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64 into the slot before the page is mapped read-only) — cl.exe-witnessed: `int (*const table[])(void)` lands in `.rdata` (0x40400040) with ADDR64 relocations. So this row is `.rdata`-CLASS under the SAME `.rdata` NAME but as its OWN row → the walker emits it as a SECOND `.rdata` section header, which COFF explicitly permits (link.exe merges same-name contributions into one image section). A distinct row (rather than folding into the rodata row) keeps the .o discipline the ELF `.data.rel.ro` / Mach-O `__DATA,__const` mirrors use: reloc-bearing rodata stays fail-loud while relro items get their own IMAGE_RELOCATION table. Characteristics (`type`) = 0x40000040 = 1073741888 — identical class to the rodata row, no align bits (walker-computed).
sections.name: .rdata

relocations.$comment: 32-bit PC-relative (call / jmp rel32). IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32 = 4. `kind` = 1 matches x86_64.target.json's `rel32` row. link.exe handles the rel32 RIP-bias intrinsically (PE convention: the patch site holds whatever bytes the assembler wrote; the linker computes `target_va - (section_va + VA + 4)` and ADDS the stored value). The assembler writes 0x00000000 at the patch site — addend=0 is the PE convention for call/jmp rel32.
relocations.name: IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32
